purpose: Sotalol is used to treat certain types of irregular heartbeats, called arrhythmias. It helps keep your heart beating in a normal, steady rhythm. Your doctor may prescribe it specifically for a condition called atrial fibrillation or other serious heart rhythm problems.
how_it_works: Sotalol works in two ways to calm down an overactive or irregular heart. It blocks certain electrical signals in the heart that can cause it to beat too fast or out of rhythm. Think of it like a traffic controller for your heart's electrical system, helping everything flow in an orderly way.
common_side_effects: You might feel tired or dizzy, especially when you first start taking it. Some people notice shortness of breath, a slower heartbeat, or feel lightheaded when standing up quickly. Nausea, headache, or cold hands and feet can also occur.
warnings: This is a very important medication — never stop taking it suddenly without talking to your doctor first, as this can be dangerous. Sotalol can actually cause a new serious heart rhythm problem in some people, so your first doses are often given in a hospital where your heart can be monitored. Tell your doctor right away if you feel your heart racing, fluttering, fainting, or if you have chest pain. It should be used carefully in people with kidney problems, asthma, or low potassium levels.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose is 80 mg taken twice a day, about 12 hours apart. Your doctor may slowly increase your dose depending on how your heart responds. It is best taken on an empty stomach. Always take it exactly as your doctor tells you and never miss a dose.
